verses.text: Di Lord talk to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, because I don harden im heart, and di heart of im servants, so that I go show dis my signs among dem,
and so that you go tell for di ears of your pikin, and of your grandpikin, wetin I don do for Egypt, and my signs wey I don do among dem, so that una go know say I na di Lord.”
Moses and Aaron go in to Pharaoh, and talk to am, “Di Lord, di God of di Hebrews, talk so: ‘How long you go refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that dem go serve me.
Or else, if you refuse to let my people go, look, tomorrow I go bring locusts into your border.

Dem go cover di surface of di earth, so that one no go fit see di earth. Dem go eat di residue of wetin escape, wey remain to una from di hail, and dem go eat every tree wey grow for una for di field.

Dem go fill your houses, and di houses of all your servants, and di houses of all di Egyptians, as neither your papa dem nor your papa dem papa dem don see, since di day wey dem dey for di earth until today.’” E turn, and go out from Pharaoh.
Pharaoh servants talk to am, “How long dis man go be snare to us? Let di men go, so that dem go serve di Lord dem God. You never know say Egypt don destroy?”
Dem bring Moses and Aaron again to Pharaoh, and e talk to dem, “Go, serve di Lord una God. But who and who go go?”
Moses talk, “We go go with our young and with our old. We go go with our pikin man dem and with our pikin woman dem, with our flocks and with our herds, because we must hold feast to di Lord.”
E talk to dem, “Make di Lord dey with una so as I go let una go, with una little ones. Look, evil dey before your face.
No so. Go now, una wey be men, and serve di Lord, because dat na wetin una dey ask.” Dem drive dem out from Pharaoh presence.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over di land of Egypt for di locusts, so that dem go come up on di land of Egypt, and eat every herb of di land, even all wey di hail don leave.”
Moses stretch out im rod over di land of Egypt, and di Lord bring one east wind on di land all dat day and all dat night. When e be morning, di east wind bring di locusts.
Di locusts go up over all di land of Egypt, and rest for all di borders of Egypt. Dem too grievous. Before dem, dere no dey locusts like dem, neither after dem go dey such.

Dem cover di surface of di whole earth, so that di land dey darkened. Dem eat every herb of di land, and all di fruit of di trees wey di hail don leave. Nothing green remain, either tree or herb of di field, through all di land of Egypt.
Den Pharaoh hurry to call Moses and Aaron, and e talk, “I don sin against di Lord una God, and against una.
Now therefore forgive my sin only dis once, and pray to di Lord una God, so that e go take away from me dis death only.”
E go out from Pharaoh, and pray to di Lord.
Di Lord turn one very strong west wind, and e take away di locusts, and throw dem into di Red Sea. No locust remain for all di borders of Egypt.
But di Lord harden Pharaoh heart, and e no let di pikin dem of Israel go.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward di sky, so that darkness go dey over di land of Egypt, even darkness wey one fit feel.”
Moses stretch out im hand toward di sky, and thick darkness dey for all di land of Egypt three days.
Dem no see one another, neither anyone rise from im place for three days, but all di pikin dem of Israel get light for dem dwellings.
Pharaoh call to Moses, and talk, “Go, serve di Lord. Only make your flocks and your herds stay behind. Make your little ones go with una too.”
Moses talk, “You must give us also sacrifices and burnt offerings, so that we go sacrifice to di Lord our God.
Our livestock go go with us too. Not one hoof go dey left behind, because we must take some of dem to serve di Lord our God. We no know wetin we go use serve di Lord until we reach dere.”
But di Lord harden Pharaoh heart, and e no agree to let dem go.
Pharaoh talk to am, “Get away from me! Beware say you no see my face again, because for di day wey you see my face, you go die.”
Moses talk, “You don talk well. I go see your face again no more.”
Di Lord talk to Moses, “I go bring one plague more on Pharaoh, and on Egypt. After dat e go let una go from here. When e go let una go, e go surely drive una out of here altogether.
Speak now for di ears of di people, make every man ask of im neighbour, and every woman of im neighbour, jewels of silver and jewels of gold.”
Di Lord give di people favour for di sight of di Egyptians. Moreover di man Moses dey very great for di land of Egypt, for di sight of Pharaoh servants, and for di sight of di people.
Moses talk, “Di Lord talk so: ‘About midnight I go go out into di middle of Egypt,
and all di firstborn for di land of Egypt go die, from di firstborn of Pharaoh wey sit on im throne, even to di firstborn of di servant wey dey behind di mill, and all di firstborn of animals.
Dere go be great cry throughout all di land of Egypt, such as no dey before, and such as no go dey again.
But against any of di pikin dem of Israel no dog go move im tongue, against man or animal, so that una go know say di Lord make distinction between di Egyptians and Israel.’
All dis your servants go come down to me, and bow down to me, talk, ‘Go out, you and all di people wey follow you,’ and after dat I go go out.” E go out from Pharaoh for hot anger.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Pharaoh no go listen to una, so that my wonders go dey multiplied for di land of Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron do all dis wonders before Pharaoh, and di Lord harden Pharaoh heart, and e no let di pikin dem of Israel go out of im land.
Di Lord speak to Moses and Aaron for di land of Egypt, talk,
“Dis month go be to una di beginning of months. E go be di first month of di year to una.
Speak to all di congregation of Israel, talk, ‘For di tenth day of dis month, dem go take to demself every man one lamb, according to di house of dem papa dem, one lamb for each household.
If di household dey too small for one lamb, make am and im neighbour next to im house take according to di number of di persons. According to every man eating, una go make una count for di lamb.
Una lamb go be without blemish, male, one year old. Una go take am from di sheep, or from di goats.
Una go keep am until di 14th day of di same month. Di whole assembly of di congregation of Israel go kill am between di two evenings.
Dem go take some of di blood, and put am on di two door posts and on di lintel, upon di houses wia dem go eat am.
Dem go eat di flesh for dat night, roasted with fire, with unleavened bread. Dem go eat am with bitter herbs.
Una no go eat any of am raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with fire, im head with im legs and with di inner parts.
Una no go leave any of am until morning, but wetin remain of am until morning una go burn with fire.
Dis na how una go eat am: with una loins girded, una sandals on una feet, and una staff for una hand. Una go eat am in haste. Na di Lord Passover.
Because I go pass through di land of Egypt dis night, and I go strike all di firstborn for di land of Egypt, both man and animal. Against all di gods of Egypt I go execute judgments. I na di Lord.
Di blood go be to una for token upon di houses wia una dey. When I see di blood, I go pass over una, and no plague go dey on una to destroy una, when I strike di land of Egypt.
Dis day go be to una for memorial, and una go keep am as feast to di Lord. Throughout una generations una go keep am as feast by perpetual ordinance.

Seven days una go eat unleavened bread. Even di first day una go put away leaven from una houses, because whoever eat leavened bread from di first day until di seventh day, dat soul go dey cut off from Israel.
For di first day una go get holy convocation, and for di seventh day one holy convocation. No kind of work go dey done for dem, except wetin every man must eat. Only dat una fit do.
Una go keep di feast of unleavened bread, because for dis very day I don bring una armies out of di land of Egypt. Therefore una go keep dis day throughout una generations by perpetual ordinance.
For di first month, for di 14th day of di month for evening, una go eat unleavened bread, until di 21st day of di month for evening.
Seven days no leaven go dey found for una houses, because whoever eat wetin dey leavened, dat soul go dey cut off from di congregation of Israel, whether e be stranger or native of di land.
Una no go eat anything leavened. For all una dwellings una go eat unleavened bread.’”
Den Moses call for all di elders of Israel, and talk to dem, “Draw out and take lambs for una according to una families, and kill di Passover.

Una go take one bunch of hyssop, and dip am for di blood wey dey di basin, and strike di lintel and di two door posts with di blood wey dey di basin. None of una go go out of di door of im house until morning.

Because di Lord go pass through to strike di Egyptians. When e see di blood on di lintel, and on di two door posts, di Lord go pass over di door, and no go allow di destroyer to come into una houses to strike una.
Una go observe dis thing as ordinance for you and for your pikin dem forever.
E go happen, when una come to di land wey di Lord go give una, as e don promise, say una go keep dis service.
E go happen, when una pikin dem talk to una, ‘Wetin dis service mean to una?’

say una go talk, ‘Na di sacrifice of di Lord Passover, wey pass over di houses of di pikin dem of Israel for Egypt, when e strike di Egyptians, and deliver our houses.’” Di people bow dem heads and worship.
Di pikin dem of Israel go away, and do am. As di Lord command Moses and Aaron, so dem do.

E come be say at midnight, di Lord strike all di firstborn for di land of Egypt, from di firstborn of Pharaoh wey sit on im throne to di firstborn of di captive wey dey di dungeon, and all di firstborn of livestock.
Pharaoh rise up for night, e, and all im servants, and all di Egyptians. Dere dey great cry for Egypt, because no house dey wia somebody no die.
E call for Moses and Aaron for night, and talk, “Rise up, go out from among my people, both una and di pikin dem of Israel. Go, serve di Lord, as una don talk.
Take your flocks and your herds too, as una don talk, and go. Bless me also.”
Di Egyptians urge di people, to send dem out of di land in haste, because dem talk, “We all go die.”
Di people take dem dough before e leaven, dem kneading bowls bound up for dem clothes on dem shoulders.
Di pikin dem of Israel do according to di word of Moses, and dem ask of di Egyptians jewels of silver, jewels of gold, and clothing.
Di Lord give di people favour for di sight of di Egyptians, so that dem give dem wetin dem ask. Dem plunder di Egyptians.
Di pikin dem of Israel journey from Rameses to Succoth, about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and little ones.
One mixed multitude go up with dem too, with flocks and herds, even very much livestock.
Dem bake unleavened cakes of di dough wey dem bring out of Egypt, because e no leavened, because dem drive dem out of Egypt, and no fit wait, neither dem prepare any food for demself.
Now di time wey di pikin dem of Israel dwell for Egypt na 430 years.
E come be say at di end of 430 years, on di very same day, all di armies of di Lord go out from di land of Egypt.
Na night to be much observed to di Lord for bringing dem out from di land of Egypt. Dis same night na di Lord own, to be much observed by all di pikin dem of Israel throughout dem generations.
Di Lord talk to Moses and Aaron, “Dis na di ordinance of di Passover: no foreigner go eat of am,
but every man servant wey dem buy for money, when you don circumcise am, e go eat of am.
One foreigner and one hired servant no go eat of am.
E go dey eaten for one house. You no go carry any of di flesh outside of di house, neither una go break any bone of am.
All di congregation of Israel go keep am.

When one stranger dey stay with you, and keep di Passover to di Lord, make all im males dey circumcised, and make am come near and keep am. E go be as one wey dey born for di land, but no uncircumcised person go eat of am.
One law go dey to di native and to di stranger wey dey stay among una.”
Na so all di pikin dem of Israel do. As di Lord command Moses and Aaron, so dem do.
E come be say di same day, di Lord bring di pikin dem of Israel out of di land of Egypt by dem armies.
Di Lord speak to Moses, talk,
“Set apart to me all di firstborn, whatever open di womb among di pikin dem of Israel, both of man and of animal. E na mine.”

Moses talk to di people, “Remember dis day, for wey una come out from Egypt, out of di house of bondage, because by strength of hand di Lord bring una out from dis place. No leavened bread go dey eaten.
Dis day una go out, for di month Abib.

E go be, when di Lord go bring you into di land of di Canaanites, di Hittites, di Amorites, di Hivites, and di Jebusites, wey e swear to your papa dem to give you, one land wey dey flow with milk and honey, say you go keep dis service for dis month.
Seven days you go eat unleavened bread, and for di seventh day go be feast to di Lord.
Unleavened bread go dey eaten for di seven days. No leavened bread go dey seen with you, neither leaven go dey seen with you for all your borders.
You go tell your pikin for dat day, talk, ‘Na because of wetin di Lord do for me when I come out of Egypt.’
E go be to you for sign on your hand, and for memorial between your eyes, so that di law of di Lord go dey for your mouth, because with strong hand di Lord bring you out of Egypt.
Therefore you go keep dis ordinance for im season from year to year.
E go be, when di Lord bring you into di land of di Canaanites, as e swear to you and to your papa dem, and give am to you,
say you go set apart to di Lord all wey open di womb, and every firstborn of animal wey you get. Di males go be di Lord own.
Every firstborn of donkey you go redeem with lamb, and if you no redeem am, you go break im neck. All di firstborn of man among your pikin dem you go redeem.
E go be, when your pikin ask you for time to come, talk, ‘Wetin dis mean?’ say you go tell am, ‘By strength of hand di Lord bring us out of Egypt, out of di house of bondage.

E come be say, when Pharaoh refuse hard to let us go, di Lord kill all di firstborn for di land of Egypt, both di firstborn of man and di firstborn of animal. Na why I sacrifice to di Lord all males wey open di womb, but all di firstborn of my pikin dem I redeem.’
E go be for sign on your hand, and for frontlets between your eyes, because by strength of hand di Lord bring us out of Egypt.”

E come be say, when Pharaoh let di people go, God no lead dem by di way of di land of di Philistines, although e near, because God talk, “Make di people no change dem mind when dem see war, and return to Egypt.”
But God lead di people around by di way of di wilderness by di Red Sea. Di pikin dem of Israel go up armed out of di land of Egypt.
Moses take di bones of Joseph with am, because Joseph don make di pikin dem of Israel swear solemnly, talk, “God go surely visit una, and una go carry up my bones from here with una.”
Dem journey from Succoth, and encamp for Etham, for di edge of di wilderness.
Di Lord go before dem by day for pillar of cloud to lead dem di way, and by night for pillar of fire to give dem light, so that dem go travel by day and by night.
Di pillar of cloud no depart by day, nor di pillar of fire by night, from before di people.
Di Lord speak to Moses, talk,
“Speak to di pikin dem of Israel, make dem turn back and encamp before Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and di sea, before Baal Zephon. Una go encamp opposite am by di sea.
Pharaoh go talk about di pikin dem of Israel, ‘Dem dey entangled for di land. Di wilderness don shut dem in.’
I go harden Pharaoh heart, and e go follow dem, and I go get honour over Pharaoh, and over all im army. Di Egyptians go know say I na di Lord.” Dem do so.
Dem tell di king of Egypt say di people don flee, and di heart of Pharaoh and of im servants turn against di people, and dem talk, “Wetin we don do, say we don let Israel go from serving us?”
E make ready im chariot, and take im people with am.
E take 600 chosen chariots, and all di other chariots of Egypt, with captains over all of dem.
Di Lord harden di heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and e pursue di pikin dem of Israel, because di pikin dem of Israel dey go out with boldness.
Di Egyptians pursue dem, all di horses and chariots of Pharaoh, im horsemen and im army, and overtake dem encamping by di sea, beside Pi Hahiroth, before Baal Zephon.
When Pharaoh draw near, di pikin dem of Israel lift up dem eyes, and look, di Egyptians dey march after dem, and dem fear greatly. Di pikin dem of Israel cry out to di Lord.
Dem talk to Moses, “Because no graves dey for Egypt, you don take us away to die for di wilderness? Why you don deal with us so, to bring us out of Egypt?
Dis no be di word wey we talk to you for Egypt, say, ‘Leave us alone, so that we go serve di Egyptians’? Because e better for us to serve di Egyptians, than to die for di wilderness.”
Moses talk to di people, “No fear. Stand still, and see di salvation of di Lord, wey e go work for una today, because di Egyptians wey una don see today, una no go see dem again forever.
Di Lord go fight for una, and una go hold una peace.”
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Why you dey cry to me? Speak to di pikin dem of Israel, make dem go forward.
Lift up your rod, stretch out your hand over di sea, and divide am, and di pikin dem of Israel go go on dry ground through di middle of di sea.
Look, I go harden di hearts of di Egyptians, and dem go follow dem, and I go get honour over Pharaoh, and over all im army, over im chariots, and over im horsemen.
Di Egyptians go know say I na di Lord, when I don get honour over Pharaoh, im chariots, and im horsemen.”
Di angel of God, wey go before di camp of Israel, remove and go behind dem, and di pillar of cloud go from before dem, and stand behind dem.
E come between di camp of Egypt and di camp of Israel. Di cloud dey dark, but e give light by night for dem. One no come near di other all night.
Moses stretch out im hand over di sea, and di Lord cause di sea to go back by one strong east wind all night, and make di sea dry land, and di waters divide.
Di pikin dem of Israel go into di middle of di sea on di dry ground, and di waters dey wall to dem on dem right hand, and on dem left.
Di Egyptians pursue, and go in after dem into di middle of di sea, all Pharaoh horses, im chariots, and im horsemen.
E come be say for di morning watch, di Lord look for di Egyptian army through di pillar of fire and of cloud, and throw di Egyptian army into confusion.
E take off dem chariot wheels, and make dem drive heavily, so that di Egyptians talk, “Make we flee from di face of Israel, because di Lord dey fight for dem against di Egyptians.”
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over di sea, so that di waters go come again on di Egyptians, on dem chariots, and on dem horsemen.”
Moses stretch out im hand over di sea, and di sea return to im strength when morning come, and di Egyptians flee against am. Di Lord overthrow di Egyptians for di middle of di sea.
Di waters return, and cover di chariots and di horsemen, even all di army of Pharaoh wey follow dem into di sea. Not so much as one of dem remain.
But di pikin dem of Israel waka on dry land through di middle of di sea, and di waters dey wall to dem on dem right hand, and on dem left.
Na so di Lord save Israel dat day out of di hand of di Egyptians. Israel see di Egyptians dead on di shore of di sea.
Israel see di great work wey di Lord do on di Egyptians, and di people fear di Lord, and dem believe di Lord and im servant Moses.
Den Moses and di pikin dem of Israel sing dis song to di Lord, and speak, talk, “I go sing to di Lord, because e don triumph gloriously. Di horse and im rider e don throw into di sea.
Di Lord na my strength and song. E don become my salvation. Dis na my God, and I go praise am, di God of my papa, and I go exalt am.
Di Lord na man of war. Di Lord na im name.
Pharaoh chariots and im army e don cast into di sea. Im chosen captains dem sink for di Red Sea.
Di deeps cover dem. Dem go down into di depths like stone.
Your right hand, Lord, dey glorious for power. Your right hand, Lord, dash di enemy to pieces.
For di greatness of your excellency, you overthrow dem wey rise up against you. You send out your wrath, e consume dem like stubble.
With di blast of your nostrils di waters pile up, di floods stand upright like one heap. Di deeps congeal for di heart of di sea.
Di enemy talk, ‘I go pursue. I go overtake. I go divide di plunder. My desire go dey satisfied for dem. I go draw my sword. My hand go destroy dem.’
You blow with your wind. Di sea cover dem. Dem sink like lead for di mighty waters.
Who dey like you, Lord, among di gods? Who dey like you, glorious for holiness, fearful for praises, doing wonders?
You stretch out your right hand. Di earth swallow dem.
By your lovingkindness you don lead di people wey you don redeem. By your strength you don guide dem to your holy habitation.
Di peoples don hear. Dem tremble. Anguish don seize di inhabitants of Philistia.
Di chiefs of Edom dey dismayed. Trembling seize di mighty men of Moab. All di inhabitants of Canaan melt away.
Terror and dread fall on dem. By di greatness of your arm dem dey still as stone, until your people pass over, Lord, until di people pass over wey you don purchase.
You go bring dem in, and plant dem for di mountain of your inheritance, di place, Lord, wey you don make for your dwelling, di sanctuary, Lord, wey your hands don establish.
Di Lord go reign forever and ever.”

Because di horses of Pharaoh go in with im chariots and with im horsemen into di sea, and di Lord bring di waters of di sea again on dem, but di pikin dem of Israel waka on dry land through di middle of di sea.
Miriam di prophetess, di sister of Aaron, take di tambourine for im hand, and all di women go out after am with tambourines and with dances.
Miriam answer dem, “Sing to di Lord, because e don triumph gloriously. Di horse and im rider e don throw into di sea.”
Moses lead Israel onward from di Red Sea, and dem go out into di wilderness of Shur. Dem go three days for di wilderness, and find no water.
When dem come to Marah, dem no fit drink di waters of Marah, because dem bitter. Na why dem call im name Marah.
Di people complain against Moses, talk, “Wetin we go drink?”
E cry to di Lord, and di Lord show am one tree. When e throw am into di waters, di waters become sweet. Dere e make for dem one statute and one ordinance, and dere e test dem.

E talk, “If you go diligently listen to di voice of di Lord your God, and go do wetin dey right for im eyes, and go listen to im commandments, and keep all im statutes, I go put none of di diseases on you, wey I don put on di Egyptians, because I na di Lord wey heal you.”
Dem come to Elim, wia 12 springs of water dey, and 70 palm trees. Dem encamp dere by di waters.

Dem take dem journey from Elim, and all di congregation of di pikin dem of Israel come to di wilderness of Sin, wey dey between Elim and Sinai, for di 15th day of di second month after dem leave di land of Egypt.
Di whole congregation of di pikin dem of Israel complain against Moses and against Aaron for di wilderness.

Di pikin dem of Israel talk to dem, “If only di Lord for don kill us for di land of Egypt, when we sit by di meat pots, when we eat bread to di full, because una don bring us out into dis wilderness, to kill dis whole assembly with hunger.”
Den di Lord talk to Moses, “Look, I go rain bread from heaven for una. Di people go go out and gather every day wetin dem need, so that I go test dem, whether dem go waka for my law or no.
E go come be say on di sixth day, dem go prepare wetin dem bring in, and e go be twice as much as dem gather every day.”
Moses and Aaron talk to all di pikin dem of Israel, “For evening, una go know say di Lord don bring una out from di land of Egypt.
For morning, una go see di glory of di Lord, because e hear una complaining against di Lord. Wetin we be, say una complain against us?”

Moses talk, “Dis go be, when di Lord go give una for evening flesh to eat, and for morning bread to di full, because di Lord hear una complaining wey una complain against am. Wetin we be? Una complaining no be against us, but against di Lord.”
Moses talk to Aaron, “Talk to all di congregation of di pikin dem of Israel, ‘Come near before di Lord, because e don hear una complaining.’”
E come be say, as Aaron speak to di whole congregation of di pikin dem of Israel, dem look toward di wilderness, and look, di glory of di Lord appear for di cloud.
Di Lord speak to Moses, talk,

“I don hear di complaining of di pikin dem of Israel. Speak to dem, talk, ‘Between di two evenings una go eat flesh, and for morning una go dey filled with bread. Una go know say I na di Lord una God.’”
E come be say for evening, di quail come up and cover di camp. For morning, one layer of dew lie round di camp.
When di layer of dew go up, look, on di surface of di wilderness dey one small round thing, small as di frost on di ground.
When di pikin dem of Israel see am, dem talk to one another, “Wetin be dis?” because dem no know wetin e be. Moses talk to dem, “Dis na di bread wey di Lord don give una to eat.

Dis na di thing wey di Lord command: ‘Gather of am every man according to wetin im need to eat, one omer for every person, according to di number of una persons. Each man go take for dem wey dey im tent.’”
Di pikin dem of Israel do so, and gather, some more, some less.
When dem measure am with omer, di one wey gather much no get too much, and di one wey gather little no lack. Every man gather according to wetin im need to eat.
Moses talk to dem, “Make nobody leave any of am until morning.”
Notwithstanding, dem no listen to Moses, but some of dem leave of am until morning, and e breed worms and stink. Moses dey angry with dem.
Dem gather am morning by morning, every man according to wetin im need to eat. When di sun grow hot, e melt.
E come be say on di sixth day, dem gather twice as much bread, two omers for each one. All di rulers of di congregation come and tell Moses.

E talk to dem, “Dis na wetin di Lord don talk: ‘Tomorrow na day of rest, di holy Sabbath to di Lord. Bake wetin una go bake, and boil wetin una go boil. All wey remain over, lay up for una to dey kept until morning.’”
Dem lay am up until morning, as Moses command, and e no stink, neither any worm dey inside am.
Moses talk, “Eat am today, because today na Sabbath to di Lord. Today una no go find am for di field.
Six days una go gather am, but on di seventh day, wey be Sabbath, e no go dey dere.”
E come be say on di seventh day, some of di people go out to gather, and dem find none.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “How long una go refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?
Look, because di Lord don give una di Sabbath, na why e give una for di sixth day di bread of two days. Make every man abide for im place. Make nobody go out of im place on di seventh day.”
So di people rest on di seventh day.
Di house of Israel call im name Manna. E dey like coriander seed, white, and di taste of am dey like wafers with honey.

Moses talk, “Dis na di thing wey di Lord command: ‘Fill one omer of am to dey kept throughout una generations, so that dem go see di bread wey I feed una with for di wilderness, when I bring una out of di land of Egypt.’”
Moses talk to Aaron, “Take one jar, put one omer full of manna inside am, and lay am up before di Lord, to dey kept throughout una generations.”
As di Lord command Moses, so Aaron lay am up before di Testimony, to dey kept.
Di pikin dem of Israel eat di manna 40 years, until dem come to one inhabited land. Dem eat di manna until dem come to di borders of di land of Canaan.
Now one omer na di tenth part of one ephah.

All di congregation of di pikin dem of Israel journey from di wilderness of Sin, by dem stages, according to di commandment of di Lord, and encamp for Rephidim. Dere no dey water for di people to drink.
Di people quarrel with Moses, and talk, “Give us water to drink.” Moses talk to dem, “Why una quarrel with me? Why una test di Lord?”
Di people thirst dere for water, and di people complain against Moses, and talk, “Why you don bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our pikin dem and our livestock with thirst?”
Moses cry to di Lord, talk, “Wetin I go do to dis people? Dem dey almost ready to stone me.”
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Go on before di people, and take with you some of di elders of Israel. Take your rod, wey you use strike di river, for your hand, and go.
Look, I go stand before you dere on di rock for Horeb. You go strike di rock, and water go come out of am, so that di people go drink.” Moses do so for di sight of di elders of Israel.
E call di name of di place Massah, and Meribah, because of di quarrel of di pikin dem of Israel, and because dem test di Lord, talk, “Di Lord dey among us, or no?”
Den Amalek come and fight with Israel for Rephidim.
Moses talk to Joshua, “Choose men for us, and go out, fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I go stand on di top of di hill with God rod for my hand.”
So Joshua do as Moses tell am, and fight with Amalek. Moses, Aaron, and Hur go up to di top of di hill.
E come be say, when Moses hold up im hand, Israel prevail, and when e let down im hand, Amalek prevail.

But Moses hands dey heavy. Dem take one stone, and put am under am, and e sit on am. Aaron and Hur support im hands, one on di one side, and di other on di other side. Im hands dey steady until di going down of di sun.
Joshua defeat Amalek and im people with di edge of di sword.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Write dis for memorial for di book, and rehearse am for di ears of Joshua: say I go utterly blot out di memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
Moses build one altar, and call im name Di Lord Na My Banner.
E talk, “Because di Lord don swear: di Lord go dey at war with Amalek from generation to generation.”
Now Jethro, di priest of Midian, Moses wife papa, hear of all wey God don do for Moses, and for Israel im people, how di Lord bring Israel out of Egypt.
Jethro, Moses wife papa, take Zipporah, Moses wife, after e don send am away,
and im two pikin man dem, of wey di name of one na Gershom, because e talk, “I don dey foreigner for strange land,”
and di name of di other na Eliezer, because e talk, “Di God of my papa na my help, and e rescue me from di sword of Pharaoh.”
Jethro, Moses wife papa, come with im pikin man dem and im wife to Moses for di wilderness wia e encamp, for di mountain of God.
E talk to Moses, “I, your wife papa Jethro, dey come to you, with your wife and im two pikin man dem with am.”
Moses go out to meet im wife papa, and e bow down and kiss am. Dem ask each other of dem welfare, and dem come into di tent.
Moses tell im wife papa all wey di Lord do to Pharaoh and to di Egyptians for Israel sake, all di hardship wey come on dem for di way, and how di Lord deliver dem.
Jethro rejoice for all di good wey di Lord don do to Israel, wey e don deliver out of di hand of di Egyptians.
Jethro talk, “Blessed be di Lord, wey don deliver una out of di hand of di Egyptians, and out of di hand of Pharaoh, wey don deliver di people from under di hand of di Egyptians.
Now I know say di Lord dey greater pass all gods, yes, for di thing wey dem deal proudly against dem.”
Jethro, Moses wife papa, take one burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron and all di elders of Israel come to eat bread with Moses wife papa before God.
E come be say di next day, Moses sit to judge di people. Di people stand around Moses from di morning to di evening.
When Moses wife papa see all wey e do for di people, e talk, “Wetin be dis thing wey you dey do to di people? Why you sit alone, and all di people stand around you from morning to evening?”
Moses talk to im wife papa, “Because di people come to me to enquire of God.
When dem get one matter, e come to me, and I judge between one and another, and I make dem know God statutes and im laws.”
Moses wife papa talk to am, “Di thing wey you dey do no good.
You go surely wear away, both you, and dis people wey dey with you, because di thing too heavy for you. You no fit perform am by yourself alone.
Listen now to my voice. I go give you counsel, and God go dey with you. You go represent di people before God, and bring di causes to God.
You go teach dem di statutes and di laws, and go show dem di way wey dem must waka, and di work wey dem must do.

Moreover you go choose out of all di people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating dishonest gain. Put dem over di people to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

Make dem judge di people at all seasons. E go be say every great matter dem go bring to you, but every small matter dem go judge demself. Dem go make am easier for you, and dem go bear di burden with you.
If you go do dis thing, and God command you so, you go fit endure, and all dis people too go go to dem place in peace.”
So Moses listen to di voice of im wife papa, and do all wey e talk.
Moses choose able men out of all Israel, and make dem heads over di people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
Dem judge di people at all seasons. Di hard cases dem bring to Moses, but every small matter dem judge demself.
Moses let im wife papa depart, and e go im way into im own land.
